task.text:
WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: It is argued that what more important school subject between history and science-related and technology disciplines. Personally, I strongly believe that both kinds of subjects have their own advantages in different aspects and what kind of subjects depends largely on each country's situation.

On the one hand, for some developed countries where science and technology are already strong, over-emphasizing science-related subjects is unnecessary. Given that in those conditions, there is a national problem that is loss of cultural identity, history gives student knowledge which help them to understand others cultural and more likely to prioritize preservation of their own heritage. Added to this is the fact that history also guide people to develop a balanced country by learning through pre-societies, leading to a long-term advancement. This can seen in the way developed countries emphasize in history.

On the other hand, for less technological advance, prioritizing science-related subject is much more beneficial. Since technology and science is the key factor that drive drive overall national development, governments should give more support to this kind of subjects. This leads to building more labours at school and there are various scientific and technological project that foster students' interest about this field. This also means help create more scientists in key fields including: healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, hence contributing to national growing. However, History is an important part, the subject without caring about the subjects, causing to an unbalanced society.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that history and science-related subjects is both important, they bring the merits in different aspects and how what subject is more important depend strongly on each country's specific background.
review.overall: Em đã chọn một quan điểm có điều kiện rõ: nước đã mạnh về khoa học có thể cần chú trọng lịch sử hơn, còn nước đang thiếu năng lực công nghệ có thể ưu tiên khoa học. Cách nhìn này trả lời được cả hai phía của đề. Tuy nhiên, em đang suy từ hoàn cảnh đất nước sang quyết định học đường quá nhanh: đoạn lịch sử cần một ví dụ cụ thể, còn đoạn khoa học cần giải thích đầu tư vào môn học tạo kỹ năng và nhân lực như thế nào. Em cũng cần viết lại những câu thiếu động từ hoặc có nhiều vế ghép lỏng để lập luận dễ theo hơn.

criteria.label: Task Response
criteria.comment: Em bàn đủ giá trị của lịch sử và khoa học/công nghệ, nêu quan điểm rõ rằng thứ tự ưu tiên tùy hoàn cảnh từng nước. Các ý về bản sắc và nhân lực có liên quan, nhưng ví dụ 'các nước phát triển chú trọng lịch sử' thiếu căn cứ và chuỗi từ đầu tư môn học đến phát triển quốc gia còn nhảy bước.

criteria.label: Coherence and Cohesion
criteria.comment: Bố cục bốn đoạn rõ, hai thân bài tách hai hoàn cảnh và kết luận quay lại lập trường. Một số câu nối bằng This/However nhưng tiền ngữ hoặc quan hệ chưa rõ; câu cuối đoạn khoa học chuyển sang mất cân bằng xã hội đột ngột.

criteria.label: Lexical Resource
criteria.comment: Em có vốn từ phù hợp cho bản sắc, di sản, phát triển quốc gia và các ngành nghề. Dù vậy, các cụm pre-societies, more labours at school, national growing và emphasize in history dùng chưa chuẩn, làm vài ý phải đoán.

criteria.label: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
criteria.comment: Em thử nhiều câu ghép và mệnh đề chỉ điều kiện, nguyên nhân, kết quả. Lỗi thiếu động từ ở câu đầu, hòa hợp chủ ngữ–động từ, dạng từ và câu nối bằng dấu phẩy xuất hiện nhiều lần; một số câu dài khó đọc trọn ý.

paragraphs.text: People debate whether history or science and technology should receive greater priority at school. In my view, both areas have distinct benefits, but the amount of attention given to each may depend on a country's needs. A school system should therefore consider its social and economic circumstances rather than apply the same priority everywhere.

On the one hand, history can be particularly valuable in a country where students are at risk of losing touch with their cultural heritage. Learning about earlier generations helps them understand how their communities developed and why certain traditions matter. For example, a class could examine local records and compare past customs with those still practised today. This gives students a concrete reason to preserve aspects of their heritage while also helping them understand other cultures. Even in a country with strong scientific education, such knowledge can add a social dimension that technical subjects alone may not provide.

On the other hand, a country with less advanced technology may have a stronger reason to invest in science-related subjects. If schools provide laboratories and practical projects, students can learn to test ideas, work with data and solve unfamiliar problems. Those skills could prepare some of them for further study and careers in healthcare, agriculture or manufacturing. More trained people in these areas may, in turn, contribute to national development. This is a possible chain of benefits rather than an automatic result of adding a subject to the timetable. Nevertheless, prioritising science should not mean removing history, since students also need to understand the society in which they will apply their skills.

In conclusion, history and science-related subjects both have important roles. History develops cultural understanding, while science and technology can strengthen practical skills. Their relative priority should depend on each country's particular needs, but students should still have the opportunity to study both.
